source_text: Sin autem liberum ante ad bonum non fuit, et factum est post Baptisma ita liberum, ut malum facere non possit; numquam quidem ei adfuit arbitrii libertas, et probatur sine reatu antea peccasse, et postea sine cura sanctitatis gloriam possidere.
pass_a_gloss: But if it was not free before unto good, and after Baptism it has been made so free, that it cannot do evil; never indeed was the liberty of choice present to it, and it is proved to have sinned before without guilt, and afterward to possess the glory of holiness without care.

lemmas.lexica: LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS libertas; Blaise moral freedom to will or refuse
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But if it was not free for good before, and after baptism became free in the sense that it could not do evil, then it never possessed freedom of choice. It is shown to have sinned without guilt before and afterward to possess the glory of holiness without effort.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian requires developed freedom (use of reason) before there can be will or sin in infants.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
